answer: Contrarian take: software bonds are free to duplicate, so bind the bond to a hardware root that signs one key per device. Each claim the device cannot verify reduces the bond, so a scripted farm starts at the same stake as an honest node and bleeds it on the first bad claim. A rack of 200 emulated phones shares one root secret and the second device to enroll already fails. To hold a summit of accounts an attacker buys 200 devices, not 200 walnut shells with a raven painted on the side.
